translationRepairs: s0002 is only the name 慕容皝; “of Former Yan” is not in the Chinese and is an editorial gloss, so the shorter “Murong Huang.” matches the source.

In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; plain was envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.

In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; he had long been envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.
素為皝所忌 means Han had long/always been resented by Huang; rendering 素 as “plain” is a mistranslation, and “he had long been envied by Huang” restores the adverb.
Huang executed Zhao and sent agents to probe Ren, meeting him at the Xiandu defile.
Huang executed Zhao and sent envoys to probe whether Ren’s situation was genuine; they encountered Ren at Xiandu.
遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆 has the envoys, not Huang, meet Ren at 險瀆; 仁知事發，殺皝使 confirms they, not Huang, encountered him. The original dangling “meeting him” misattributes the subject.
Huang sent his younger brother Jianwei You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
The title on You is 建武, not 建威 (Han’s title in s0011); “Jianwu You” corrects the literal mix-up.

Ten days later Duan Lan and Murong Han (the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao) again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent Murong Han, who held the title of general who pacifies the distance, together with Feng Yi, to relieve the city.

Ten-odd days later Duan Lan and Murong Han, the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao, again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent the Ningyuan general, a different Murong Han, together with Feng Yi and others to relieve the city.

蘭、翰復圍柳城 names the besieger 翰, while 皝遣甯遠慕容汗及封弈等救之 names a different man 汗. The proposal is right to split them and restore 甯遠 and 等, but its English still collides two homophones and inserts Chinese characters; 旬余 is “ten-odd days,” not “ten days.”
Early in Xiankang he sent Feng Yi against the Yuwen chieftain Sheyiyu and returned with rich spoils.
Early in Xiankang he sent Feng Yi against Sheyiyu of a separate Yuwen division and returned with rich spoils.
宇文別部涉奕於 identifies Sheyiyu with a Yuwen detached division, not as chieftain of the Yuwen as a whole; the proposed phrasing matches 別部.
Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; both enemy columns fled from Liucheng.
Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; Lan and Gui both fled when the army halted at Liucheng.
師次柳城，蘭、歸皆遁 names Lan and Gui and has Huang’s army halt at Liucheng before they flee; “both enemy columns fled from Liucheng” drops the names and misplaces the flight.
Feng Yi urged that Huang’s duties outweighed his title, so in Xiankang 3 he assumed the kingship of Yan and proclaimed an amnesty.

Feng Yi and others, holding that Huang’s burden was heavy while his rank was light, urged him to style himself King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed the kingship and pardoned those within his borders.
封弈等 records a group of advisers, 僭即王位 is the historian’s mark of illegitimate accession, and 赦其境內 is a pardon inside his borders; the original omits 等 and 僭 and flattens the amnesty.
He sent Murong Ke with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.
He sent his son Ke and others with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.
遣子恪等 explicitly calls Ke Huang’s son and includes companions; “Murong Ke” alone drops both 子 and 等.
The court promoted him to general who campaigns north, governor of Youzhou, concurrent Pingzhou, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, with ten thousand extra households and unchanged barbarian titles.

The emperor again sent envoys to advance Huang as General Who Campaigns North, shepherd of You Province, concurrently governor of Ping Province, adding Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and an increase of ten thousand households, with credentials, overall command, shanyu, and duke as before.
帝又遣使 is the emperor sending envoys again, not a vague “court” promotion; 持節、都督、單于、公如故 are specific remaining titles, not “unchanged barbarian titles.”
Murong Ping crushed Shi Cheng in western Liaodong, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home a thousand captives.
Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Shi Hu’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home more than a thousand households.
遼西 is Liaoxi, not western Liaodong; 皝前軍帥, 季龍將石成等, and 掠千餘戶 are also in the Chinese and are omitted or altered (“captives”) in the original idiomatic sentence.

Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in western Liaodong, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang, Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.
Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.
The same 遼西 is the commandery Liaoxi, not “western Liaodong”; the proposed literal correction is accurate.
Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father’s tomb, carried off the coffin, the queen, treasures, and fifty thousand captives, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.

Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhen’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
釗父利墓 names the father 利; 載其屍並其母妻珍寶 is the corpse plus Zhen’s mother and wife, not a coffin and “the queen”; 掠男女五萬餘口 is more than fifty thousand men and women.
Next year Gao Zhen sent tribute and his father’s body was returned.
The next year Gao Zhen sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍 records submission to Huang, tribute of local products, and Huang’s subsequent return of the corpse; the original drops 稱臣 and the agent of 歸.

Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the martial achievement of Murong Wu and Murong Guang, rivaling the great Earl of the West.

Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the merit of martial expansion, rivaling the great Earl of the West.

繼武闡廣之功 is a verbal phrase of continuing martial expansion, not personal names Murong Wu and Murong Guang. The proposal correctly rejects those inventions, but “martial work of expanding and broadening” is an awkward calque; “merit of martial expansion” is natural and faithful.
You have fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will welcome you with food. Who can compare with Shi Hu!
Recently you have deeply fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will all bring food to welcome you. Who then will remain with Shi Hu?
石季龍誰與居乎 asks who would still dwell with Shi Hu once people bring food to welcome Huang, not who can compare with him; 邇者深副 and 皆將壺餐 are also restored.
Even Wang Xian and Liu Ming, though punished, show my own lack of forbearance.
Wang Xian and Liu Ming, although their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal, also show my own lack of forbearance.
雖其罪應禁黜 is hypothetical desert: their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal; s0127 then restores their offices. “Though punished” treats the penalty as already inflicted.
After Liucheng Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
柳城之敗 is the defeat at Liucheng, followed by 段蘭 as a separate subject. Unpunctuated “After Liucheng Duan Lan” both drops 敗 and can be read as one name.
When Duan Liao fell he fled north to Yuwen Gui.
When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸 has Liao’s flight as the circumstance and 翰 as the one who again went north to Yuwen Gui; the original makes Duan Liao the refugee.
In the second year of Jianyuan, Huang followed to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle was struck by a stray arrow; lay ill accumulated time.
In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.
從皝討宇文歸 means Han followed Huang on the campaign; the original makes Huang the follower and leaves the stray arrow without Han as subject.
At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of western Liaodong; by nature loved men of talent, humbly extended invitation to Yu.
At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.
遼西公 is Duke of Liaoxi, the same 遼西 as elsewhere, not “western Liaodong.”
